verdict.rationale: pnpm's GitHub README states it supports Windows, Linux, and macOS. The docs describe portable project-level setup: a self-contained executable, per-project Node.js pinning that avoids 'works on my machine' mismatches, automatic version switching via the packageManager field, and env-variable substitution in config files. One community report notes some `pnpx create` scripts misbehaving in Windows Terminal, a minor edge case rather than a contradiction. Missing for 10: in-depth first-party docs on cross-platform behavior and config parity, independent hands-on corroboration of identical workflows across all three OSes.

support.subject: As a developer, I can use the same workflow and config on macOS, Linux, and Windows

citations.quote: Works everywhere. Supports Windows, Linux, and macOS.
Install and pin Node.js per project straight from pnpm — no nvm, no shell hooks, no “works on my machine” version mismatches.
pnpm is a self-contained executable, and it can install the runtime for you afterwards
If your `package.json` has a `packageManager` or `devEngines.packageManager` field, pnpm switches to that version on first use
